title: Why People With Great Talent Are Commonly Ambitious
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article traces the origins of ambition in highly talented people to a self-reinforcing cycle: early success produces a view of what's possible, generates recognition, and encourages further investment in skill development, which produces more success and internalizes a high-achiever identity. It notes that talented people also tend to compare themselves to strong peers, which raises their own internal standards over time. The piece concludes that ambition is mostly a learned attitude shaped by family expectations, role models, and rewarded effort rather than pure personality, and advises leaders selecting talent to look for ambition as a strong, related signal of ability.
points: Early success builds a self-view of what's possible, which triggers recognition and reinforces investment in skill development.
Talented people tend to compare themselves to strong peers, which raises their own internal standards over time.
Ambition is mostly a learned attitude, shaped by family expectations, role models, and rewarded effort, not fixed personality.
Leaders selecting talent should treat high ambition as a related and useful signal of underlying ability.
quotes: Many of the most talented team members are unusually ambitious.
High ability at a young age or at school produces a view of what is possible.
Highly talented people are more likely to compare themselves to strong peers.
contrary to popular wisdom, ambition is mostly a learned attitude .
In most cases, ambition and talent are two sides of the same coin.
